questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical knowledge of Azure AD application lifecycle management, including app registration, group-based access control, security policies, and automated governance for time-limited pilots.

## Key Concepts
- App Registrations and App Roles for granular access control
- Enterprise Applications and group-based permissions
- Conditional Access policies (MFA, location-based restrictions)
- Access Reviews for automated access lifecycle management
- Validation procedures and rollback planning

## Code Example
```bash
# Create app registration
az ad app create --display-name "PilotApp" --sign-in-audience AzureADMyOrg

# Create service principal
az ad sp create --id <app-id>

# Create pilot group
az ad group create --display-name "PilotGroup" --mail-nickname "pilotgroup"

# Assign group to enterprise application
az ad app permission add --id <app-id> --api-permissions <permission-id>=Role

# Create conditional access policy (requires Azure AD Premium P2)
az ad ca policy create --display-name "PilotApp MFA Policy"
```

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical knowledge of Azure AD PIM, including JIT elevation, approval workflows, MFA enforcement, and incident response within real-world identity governance frameworks.

## Key Concepts
- Azure AD Privileged Identity Management (PIM)
- Just-in-Time elevation and activation windows
- Approval workflows and MFA enforcement
- Audit logs, SIEM integration, and anomaly detection
- Sandbox validation and rollback/auto-revocation mechanisms
- Testing plans and production readiness criteria

## Code Example
```bash
# Connect to Azure AD
Connect-AzureAD

# Enable PIM for a specific role
$role = Get-AzureADMSPrivilegedRoleDefinition -ProviderId aadRoles -ResourceId $tenantId | Where-Object { $_.DisplayName -eq 'Global Administrator' }

# Assign a user as eligible with time-bound activation
Open-AzureADMSPrivilegedRoleAssignmentRequest -ProviderId aadRoles -RoleDefinitionId $role.Id -ResourceId $tenantId -SubjectId $userId -AssignmentType User -Type AdminAdd -Reason 'JIT access for contractor' -Duration 'PT4H' -ApprovalId $approvalWorkflowId

# Verify MFA enforcement in activation settings
Set-AzureADMSPrivilegedRoleSetting -ProviderId aadRoles -ResourceId $tenantId -RoleDefinitionId $role.Id -UserMemberSettings $activationSettings
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates your understanding of cross-tenant delegation, least-privilege access principles, and end-to-end governance controls.

## Key Concepts
- Azure Lighthouse managed service offers
- Scoped RBAC with granular resource guards
- Conditional Access policies (MFA, device posture compliance)
- Activity auditing via Azure Monitor and Log Analytics
- Time-bounded access with automatic expiration
- Rollback and cleanup procedures

## Code Example
```powershell
# Create Lighthouse offer with scoped access
az deployment mg create \
  --location eastus \
  --managed-by-tenant-id <partner-tenant-id> \
  --authorizations '{"principalId":"<principal-id>","roleDefinitionId":"<role-id>","principalIdDisplayName":"Partner Access"}'

# Assign with time-bound expiration
az role assignment create \
  --scope /subscriptions/<sub-id>/resourceGroups/<rg-name> \
  --assignee-object-id <partner-object-id> \
  --roleDefinitionName "Reader" \
  --assignee-valid-from $(date -u +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ") \
  --assignee-valid-until $(date -u -d "+30 days" +"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")

# Cleanup on expiry
az role assignment delete --scope /subscriptions/<sub-id>/resourceGroups/<rg-name> --assignee-object-id <partner-object-id>
```

Why This Is Asked
Tests practical IAM design for multi-service Azure AD setups, focusing on fine-grained access control and lifecycle management.

Key Concepts
- Per-service app registrations and app roles
- Just-in-time access with PIM and dynamic groups
- Conditional Access for service principals
- Automated access reviews and time-bound revocation
- Sandbox validation and rollback planning

Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo: obtain token for a service and call a resource
const token = await acquireToken({scope: 'api://svc1/.default'});
const res = await fetch('https://api.example/svc1', {headers: {Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`}});
console.log(res.status);
```

Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle token lifetimes and caching in a distributed system?
- How would you test CA policy changes without affecting production?
